input:
The ISP pipeline drops frames sporadically (roughly 1 in every 200 frames) and the drops are always preceded by a PLL unlock event in the kernel log:

  [  234.112] clk: mtk-clk-mt6989: mmsys_pll: unlock event detected (jitter threshold exceeded)
  [  234.113] clk: mtk-clk-mt6989: mmsys_pll: re-locking... done in 18us
  [  234.114] mtk-csi: csi0: MIPI D-PHY clock lane: byte_clk error, cnt=1
  [  234.115] mtk-isp: pipe_1: input underrun: no data from CSI during frame 4412
  [  234.116] mtk-isp: pipe_1: dropping frame 4412 (underrun)

The PLL re-locks in 18 us, but during that 18 us window the MIPI CSI-2 byte clock is disrupted, causing an input underrun on the ISP. The mmsys_pll drives both the CSI byte clock and the ISP pixel clock. I believe the jitter threshold is being exceeded due to NoC load spikes when other subsystems initiate high-bandwidth DMA. How do I confirm that NoC load is the cause of PLL jitter, and what is the recommended mitigation for decoupling PLL stability from bus load?
